- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

Details:
- Initially, align invokes `H.process_current_region`, using the global
  or buffer local config values. Unless the user changed
  `config.options.split_pattern`, that initial call will not result in
  changed lines.

  Currently, those lines are written to the buffer. The buffer is marked
  as changed, which confuses the user as there are no changes. Also, if
  the user stops the process, the buffer is still marked as modified.

- Solution: Only write to buffer if lines were changed.

I included an extra commit, adding `i` and `|` modifiers to the `setup` test.

~~Also, in `:h MiniAlign.config`, I wonder if the [example](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/174eb9b9d5d66254966b9d52ea51b996317e51f6/doc/mini-align.txt#L508) for the default `i` modifier is correct. Perhaps `MiniAlign.gen_step.ignore_split()` should be added to the `config.steps.pre_split` table, similar like [this](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/174eb9b9d5d66254966b9d52ea51b996317e51f6/doc/mini-align.txt#L561) example.~~

comment_data.body: I've just realized that this is probably not entirely full proof: `{ 'a ', 'b' }` and `{ 'a', ' b' }` will be computed as not changed. It is better either `vim.deep_equal()` or use `table.concat(string, '\n')`.
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -1680,13 +1679,17 @@ H.process_current_region = function(lines_were_changed, mode, opts, steps)
   -- Actually process region
   local strings = H.region_get_text(region, mode)
   local strings_aligned = MiniAlign.align_strings(strings, opts, steps)
-  H.region_set_text(region, mode, strings_aligned)
 
-  -- Make sure that latest changes are shown
-  vim.cmd('redraw')
+  -- Set text if lines changed
+  local lines_changed = table.concat(strings) ~= table.concat(strings_aligned)

comment_data.body: I don't think this is an equivalent change if `H.process_current_region` doesn't use `lines_were_changed` in a similar manner. Currently `lines_were_changed` tracks whether the lines were set at least once, while here it tracks whether it was changed on the latest iteration. Is this necessary?
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -806,9 +806,8 @@ MiniAlign.align_user = function(mode)
     opts = H.normalize_opts(opts)
     steps = H.normalize_steps(steps, opts)
 
-    -- Process region while tracking if lines were set at least once
-    local lines_now_changed = H.process_current_region(lines_were_changed, mode, opts, steps)
-    lines_were_changed = lines_were_changed or lines_now_changed
+    -- Process region while tracking if lines were changed
+    lines_were_changed = H.process_current_region(lines_were_changed, mode, opts, steps)

comment_data.body:
This is not immediately obvious that the test is for "nothing has changed", since the `changedtick` *has* changed. The main problem is that the buffer is marked as modified, so that should be tested. Would require "unwrapping" `validate_keys` to also include `child.bo.modified = false` after `set_lines`.

Also I'd verify this as `eq(child.b.changedtick. start_tick + 1)`.
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -1342,8 +1342,11 @@ T['Align']['stops on `<Esc>` and `<C-c>`'] = function()
   -- <C-c> should stop even if it doesn't make `getcharstr` error
   child.cmd('nnoremap <C-c> <C-\\><C-n>')
   for _, stop_key in ipairs({ '<Esc>', '<C-c>' }) do
+    local start_tick = child.b.changedtick
     validate_keys({ 'a\3b', 'aa\3b' }, { 'ga', 'ip', stop_key }, { 'a\3b', 'aa\3b' })
     eq(get_mode(), 'n')
+    -- Verify clean stop
+    eq(child.b.changedtick - start_tick, 1)

comment_data.body: The same as in the previous test case: `eq(child.bo.modified, false)` is probably a more accurate test for what is the actual problem.
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -1609,7 +1612,12 @@ T['Align with preview']['stops preview after `<Esc>` and `<C-c>`'] = function()
     local lines = { 'a_b', 'aa_b' }
     set_lines(lines)
     set_cursor(1, 0)
-    type_keys(init_keys, '_')
+    -- Unchanged text should not be written to buffer
+    local start_tick = child.b.changedtick
+    type_keys(init_keys)
+    eq(child.b.changedtick, start_tick)

comment_data.body:
Yes, I think so. 

Variable `lines_were_changed` is used to call `H.undo()`. When only *changed* lines are written, it needs to reflect the latest iteration. 
Otherwise, when `lines_were_changed` keeps being true after lines where set at least once, `undo` might be called even when no lines were written...

~~That would happen initially with the default config~~, but also in an interactive session when the user for example reverts the split back to ``. See also [this](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/174eb9b9d5d66254966b9d52ea51b996317e51f6/tests/test_align.lua#L2054) test.
